devsecops_best_practices.overview: Security best practices for implementing TLS/mTLS/OAuth in regulated banking environments. These practices eliminate hidden risks from framework abstractions while maintaining development velocity and ensuring compliance.

practice.rule: Use TLS 1.3 as the preferred protocol version
practice.rationale: TLS 1.3 provides improved security, performance, and removes legacy cryptographic algorithms. It's the current industry standard.

implementation.bad: # Allowing weak protocols ssl_protocols TLSv1 TLSv1.1 TLSv1.2;

practice.rule: TLS 1.2 is the minimum acceptable version for legacy compatibility
practice.rationale: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated and have known vulnerabilities. Banking regulations typically prohibit their use.
practice.exceptions: Only allow TLS 1.2 when TLS 1.3 compatibility issues exist with legacy systems. Document and track these exceptions.

practice.rule: Disable SSL 2.0 and SSL 3.0 completely
practice.rationale: These protocols have critical vulnerabilities (POODLE, DROWN) and must never be enabled.

practice.rule: Use only AEAD cipher suites (GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305)
practice.rationale: Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) provides both confidentiality and integrity in a single operation.

practice.rule: Disable CBC mode cipher suites
practice.rationale: CBC mode is vulnerable to padding oracle attacks (BEAST, Lucky13). AEAD modes are superior.

prohibited_ciphers.cipher: Any cipher with CBC in the name

practice.rule: Enable Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS)
practice.rationale: PFS ensures that session keys cannot be compromised even if the server's private key is later compromised.
practice.implementation: Use ECDHE (Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman Ephemeral) key exchange. Avoid static RSA key exchange.

practice.rule: Use certificates from trusted Certificate Authorities only
practice.rationale: Self-signed certificates are acceptable only in development/testing. Production must use trusted CAs for client trust and compliance.

practice.rule: Minimum RSA key size of 2048 bits, prefer 3072 or 4096 bits
practice.rationale: 2048-bit RSA is the current minimum standard. 3072+ bits provides better long-term security and quantum resistance.

key_recommendations.recommendation: ECDSA P-256 or P-384 for performance-critical services

practice.rule: Certificate validity period maximum 397 days (13 months)
practice.rationale: Industry standard (CA/Browser Forum) limits certificate lifetime. Shorter lifetimes reduce exposure window if compromised.
practice.automation: Implement automated certificate renewal at least 30 days before expiration.

practice.rule: Implement certificate pinning for critical services
practice.rationale: Prevents man-in-the-middle attacks using rogue certificates. Essential for mobile apps and high-security APIs.
practice.implementation: Pin to intermediate CA certificate or public key hash, not leaf certificate.

practice.rule: Enable OCSP stapling for certificate revocation checking
practice.rationale: Improves performance and privacy while maintaining revocation checking.

practice.rule: Use separate certificates for different services/domains
practice.rationale: Limits blast radius if a certificate is compromised. Enables independent rotation schedules.

practice.rule: Always verify client certificates in mTLS configurations
practice.rationale: mTLS provides mutual authentication. Failing to verify client certificates defeats the purpose.

implementation.bad: # Optional verification is not mTLS ssl_verify_client optional;

practice.rule: Implement proper certificate revocation checking (CRL or OCSP)
practice.rationale: Client certificates may be compromised or revoked. Must check revocation status before accepting.

practice.rule: Use separate CA for client certificates vs server certificates
practice.rationale: Separation of concerns. Compromised client CA doesn't affect server certificate trust.

practice.rule: Implement certificate-based authorization, not just authentication
practice.rationale: Verify not just that the certificate is valid, but that the certificate holder is authorized for the requested operation.
practice.implementation: Extract certificate subject DN or SAN and map to authorization policies.

practice.rule: Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)
practice.rationale: Forces browsers to use HTTPS, preventing protocol downgrade attacks.

implementation.good: # nginx HSTS header add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload" always;

hsts_requirements.requirement: max-age of at least 1 year (31536000 seconds)

practice.rule: Disable TLS compression to prevent CRIME attacks
practice.rationale: TLS compression can leak information through compression ratio analysis.

implementation.good: # nginx - compression disabled by default ssl_compression off;

practice.rule: Disable TLS session tickets for high-security environments
practice.rationale: Session tickets can compromise Perfect Forward Secrecy if not properly managed.
practice.exceptions: Session tickets acceptable if keys are rotated frequently and securely distributed across load balancers.

practice.rule: Use Authorization Code flow with PKCE for all client types
practice.rationale: PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) prevents authorization code interception attacks. Required for public clients, recommended for all.

practice.rule: Never use Implicit flow or Resource Owner Password Credentials flow
practice.rationale: These flows are deprecated due to security vulnerabilities. OAuth 2.1 removes them entirely.

practice.rule: Always validate the state parameter to prevent CSRF
practice.rationale: State parameter prevents cross-site request forgery attacks on the OAuth callback.
practice.implementation: Generate cryptographically random state value, store in session, validate on callback.

practice.rule: Use exact string matching for redirect URI validation
practice.rationale: Loose matching (substring, regex) can be exploited for open redirects.

practice.rule: Never allow wildcard or dynamic redirect URIs
practice.rationale: Wildcards enable attackers to redirect to malicious sites.

practice.rule: Use HTTPS for all redirect URIs in production
practice.rationale: HTTP redirect URIs expose authorization codes to network attackers.
practice.exceptions: localhost HTTP allowed only for development/testing.

practice.rule: Use short-lived access tokens (15 minutes or less)
practice.rationale: Limits exposure window if token is compromised.

practice.rule: Implement refresh token rotation
practice.rationale: Detects token theft. If old refresh token is used after rotation, revoke all tokens for that user.
practice.implementation: Issue new refresh token with each refresh request, invalidate old one.

practice.rule: Store tokens securely - never in localStorage
practice.rationale: localStorage is accessible to JavaScript, vulnerable to XSS.

secure_storage.option: HttpOnly, Secure cookies (best for web apps)
Secure device storage (iOS Keychain, Android Keystore)
Memory only (for SPAs, with refresh token in HttpOnly cookie)

practice.rule: Implement token introspection for resource servers
practice.rationale: Validates token is still active and not revoked.
practice.implementation: Resource servers should call token introspection endpoint or validate JWT signature and claims.

practice.rule: Use opaque tokens for access tokens, JWTs for ID tokens
practice.rationale: Opaque tokens prevent information disclosure and enable centralized revocation. JWTs appropriate for ID tokens with signature validation.

practice.rule: Implement principle of least privilege for scopes
practice.rationale: Grant only the minimum scopes necessary for the application's function.
practice.implementation: Define granular scopes (read:account, write:transactions) rather than broad scopes (admin, full_access).

practice.rule: Validate scopes on every API request
practice.rationale: Token may have been issued with broader scopes than endpoint requires. Always verify.

practice.rule: Implement consent screens for sensitive scopes
practice.rationale: Users must explicitly approve access to sensitive data.

practice.rule: Use client_secret_post or client_secret_jwt for confidential clients
practice.rationale: More secure than client_secret_basic (HTTP Basic Auth).

implementation.good:
// Client secret in POST body POST /token Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
grant_type=authorization_code& code=...& client_id=...& client_secret=...

practice.rule: Rotate client secrets regularly (every 90 days)
practice.rationale: Limits exposure window if secret is compromised.
practice.automation: Implement automated secret rotation with overlap period for zero-downtime updates.

practice.rule: Use private_key_jwt for high-security clients
practice.rationale: Asymmetric authentication is more secure than shared secrets.
practice.implementation: Client signs JWT with private key, authorization server validates with public key.

practice.rule: Use SHA-256 or SHA-384 for hashing, never MD5 or SHA-1
practice.rationale: MD5 and SHA-1 have known collision vulnerabilities.

practice.rule: Use AES-256-GCM for symmetric encryption
practice.rationale: AES-256 with GCM mode provides both confidentiality and integrity.

implementation.bad: // Weak - ECB mode, no authentication Cipher cipher = Cipher.getInstance("AES/ECB/PKCS5Padding");

practice.rule: Plan for post-quantum cryptography migration
practice.rationale: Quantum computers will break current public-key cryptography. Start planning now for long-term data protection.

migration_steps.step: Inventory all cryptographic usage (use IBM Quantum Safe Explorer)
Identify data with long-term confidentiality requirements

practice.rule: Never hardcode cryptographic keys or secrets in code
practice.rationale: Hardcoded secrets are easily discovered and cannot be rotated.

secure_alternatives.alternative: Secrets management service (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager)
Hardware Security Module (HSM) for critical keys

practice.rule: Implement key rotation policies
practice.rationale: Regular rotation limits exposure if key is compromised.

rotation_schedule.key_type: TLS private keys: Every 1-2 years (with certificate)

practice.rule: Use separate keys for different purposes
practice.rationale: Key separation limits blast radius and enables independent rotation.

separation_examples.example: Separate keys for encryption vs signing
Separate keys per environment (dev, staging, prod)
Separate keys per data classification level

practice.rule: Implement secure key generation with sufficient entropy
practice.rationale: Weak random number generation leads to predictable keys.

practice.rule: Use bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2 for password hashing
practice.rationale: These algorithms are designed for password hashing with built-in salting and computational cost.

implementation.good: // Spring Security - bcrypt PasswordEncoder encoder = new BCryptPasswordEncoder(12);
implementation.bad: // Weak - fast hash, no salt String hash = DigestUtils.sha256Hex(password);

practice.rule: Never log, display, or transmit passwords in plaintext
practice.rationale: Passwords must be protected at all times.

protection_measures.measure: Redact from logs and error messages

practice.rule: Explicitly configure security rather than relying on auto-configuration
practice.rationale: Auto-configuration may have insecure defaults or unexpected behavior.

practice.rule: Validate SSL bundle configurations explicitly
practice.rationale: Spring Boot SSL bundles abstract TLS configuration. Must verify actual settings match requirements.

validation_steps.step: Verify certificate paths and key stores
Confirm protocol versions and cipher suites

practice.rule: Validate templated configurations before deployment
practice.rationale: Ansible/Terraform templates may resolve to insecure values.

validation_approach.step: Render templates with actual variable values
Scan rendered output for security issues

practice.rule: Use immutable infrastructure patterns
practice.rationale: Prevents configuration drift and ensures consistency.
practice.implementation: Build complete images/containers with configuration baked in. Replace rather than update in place.

pitfall.name: assuming_framework_defaults_are_secure
pitfall.description: Frameworks prioritize ease of use over security. Default configurations often allow weak protocols or ciphers for compatibility.
pitfall.impact: Production systems may have insecure TLS configurations
pitfall.prevention: Always explicitly configure security settings. Never rely on defaults. Validate with runtime testing.

pitfall.name: incomplete_certificate_validation
pitfall.description: Disabling certificate validation for testing and forgetting to re-enable.
pitfall.prevention: Use separate configuration for dev/test/prod. Never disable validation in production. Use feature flags with strict controls.

pitfall.name: oauth_redirect_uri_validation_bypass
pitfall.description: Using loose matching (startsWith, contains) for redirect URI validation.
pitfall.impact: Open redirect vulnerability, authorization code theft
pitfall.prevention: Use exact string matching only. Pre-register all redirect URIs.

pitfall.name: token_storage_in_localstorage
pitfall.description: Storing OAuth tokens in browser localStorage.
pitfall.prevention: Use HttpOnly, Secure cookies or memory-only storage with refresh token in HttpOnly cookie.

pitfall.name: missing_runtime_validation
pitfall.description: Assuming deployment configuration matches intent without testing.
pitfall.prevention: Always perform runtime validation with testssl.sh, SSLyze, or similar tools after deployment.

pitfall.name: certificate_expiration_surprises
pitfall.prevention: Implement automated monitoring with alerts 30+ days before expiration. Automate renewal process.

Identify all TLS/mTLS endpoints and OAuth flows
Document approved algorithms, protocols, and configurations
Plan certificate management and rotation strategy

category.name: during_implementation
category.item: Use approved cryptographic libraries and algorithms
Explicitly configure security settings (no defaults)
Implement proper error handling without information disclosure
Add security-focused logging for audit trail
Document security decisions and trade-offs

category.name: before_deployment
category.item: Run static analysis and IaC security scans
Perform cryptographic visibility analysis
Validate resolved configurations
Review and approve security findings

category.name: after_deployment
category.item: Perform runtime TLS/mTLS validation
Test OAuth flows with security scanner
Verify certificate chains and validity
Confirm monitoring and alerting is active
Generate compliance evidence package

category.name: ongoing
category.item: Monitor for configuration drift
Track certificate expiration dates
Review cryptographic posture regularly
Update security controls as threats evolve
Maintain audit trail of all changes
